features.feature_value: Used a civil-forum standard: remove when it crosses into toxicity (slurs/ad hominem), keep when substantive.
features.rationale: The participant explicitly describes a rule distinguishing substantive debate from toxicity and dehumanizing language.

features.feature_value: Removed posts with name-calling or unnecessary expletives; aimed to be “do no harm.”
features.evidence_span: disallowed anything that included name-calling or unnecessary expletives
features.rationale: They cite specific linguistic markers (name-calling, expletives) as removal triggers.

features.feature_value: Removed the clearly hateful items; when one was “good” and the other “bad,” they weighed whether to delete both or keep for the support of one comment.
features.rationale: They describe how they treated hate speech differently and how they handled mixed valence within a pair.

features.feature_value: Removal choices focused on whether language was flammatory enough to shut down healthy discussion.
features.evidence_span: flammatory language that would shut down healthy discussion
features.rationale: They directly connect the removal rationale to discussion-dampening inflammatory language.

features.feature_value: Kept based on free-speech but removed when it became too offensive and unnecessary; censorship viewed as generally undesirable.
features.evidence_span: when it got too offensive and unneccisary
features.rationale: They articulate an affective/values-based threshold for offensiveness while noting the preference not to censor.

features.feature_value: Tried to stay objective; looked for statements that were untrue or inane in addition to discouraging insults/expletives.
features.evidence_span: watched for statements that were untrue and those that were inane
features.rationale: They describe a specific evaluation process including truthfulness/meaningfulness checks.

features.feature_value: Judged the “flow of the perspective” and removed when it became cursing to curse rather than constructive discussion.
features.evidence_span: based on the flow of the perspective, whether it was constructive or just cursing to curse
features.rationale: They indicate a comparative/transformative criterion (constructive vs devolving into cursing) rather than purely topical reasons.

features.feature_value: Used a contribution-to-healthy-debate check; if unsure, they typically did not remove.
features.evidence_span: If I wasn't sure, I typically decided not to remove them.
features.rationale: They state a decision rule tied to uncertainty and whether the post supports healthy political debate.
